body:
Gujarat within the Mauryan political world

The history of the Mauryan Empire has an important connection with present-day Gujarat, particularly the Girnar region near Junagadh in Saurashtra.

The region preserves evidence associated with Mauryan authority and administration. Two particularly important subjects are the Ashokan rock inscriptions at Girnar and the historical record of the Sudarshana Lake.

The Girnar rock inscriptions

Near Junagadh, a large rock contains important inscriptions from different periods of Indian history.

The earliest major group consists of 14 Major Rock Edicts of Ashoka, written in Prakrit using the Brahmi script.

These inscriptions provide direct evidence of Ashoka's communication of royal instructions and dhamma in the western part of the Mauryan Empire.

The same rock also carries later inscriptions associated with Rudradaman I and Skandagupta. These were rulers of different dynasties in later centuries.

Therefore, the inscriptions at Girnar are not all Mauryan inscriptions. They are records from different historical periods preserved at the same location.

Sudarshana Lake: Evidence of Mauryan administration

Sudarshana Lake was an artificial reservoir associated with the Girnar region of Gujarat. Its history is known particularly through the later Junagadh inscription of Rudradaman I.

Construction during Chandragupta Maurya's reign

According to the inscription, the reservoir was originally constructed by Pushyagupta, a provincial governor serving during the reign of Chandragupta Maurya.

This connection is significant because it places an important public water-management project in Gujarat within the period of early Mauryan rule.

Improvement during Ashoka's reign

The inscription also records that Tushaspha, a governor during the reign of Ashoka, improved the reservoir through the construction of water channels.

Thus, the lake's development was associated with more than 1 Mauryan ruler and with provincial officials working in the Girnar region.

Repairs by later rulers

In approximately 150 CE, the Western Kshatrapa ruler Rudradaman I recorded the repair of the reservoir after damage caused by a severe storm.

A later inscription records another repair during the reign of Skandagupta in the 5th century CE.

These later repairs demonstrate the continued importance of the water-management structure after Mauryan rule had ended. They do not make Rudradaman or Skandagupta members of the Mauryan dynasty.

What the Gujarat evidence establishes

The Girnar inscriptions and Sudarshana Lake record illustrate 2 different but related aspects of imperial authority.

  • Royal communication: Ashoka's edicts demonstrate the transmission of imperial instructions and moral principles to the western regions.
  • Provincial administration: The activities attributed to Pushyagupta and Tushaspha demonstrate the association of provincial governors with public works in the Girnar region.

Together, these records support the identification of Saurashtra as a region connected with Mauryan political authority.

Pushyagupta is associated with the original construction of Sudarshana Lake under Chandragupta Maurya. Tushaspha is associated with improvements under Ashoka. Rudradaman I and Skandagupta belong to later periods.

The complete transition from Nanda state to Mauryan empire

The political history covered in this lesson follows a connected sequence. Magadha first became powerful because of its agricultural resources, geographical position and expanding political organisation. The Nandas strengthened the resulting territorial state through extensive revenue collection, a substantial army and further expansion.

Chandragupta Maurya replaced the Nandas and founded a larger empire around 321 BCE. His north-western expansion and the agreement with Seleucus consolidated Mauryan authority over important frontier regions. Bindusara maintained the empire, while Ashoka inherited this political structure and subsequently conquered Kalinga.

After the Kalinga war, Ashoka increasingly emphasised dhamma-vijaya as a means of extending moral influence and promoting social coexistence. Political authority, however, continued to depend on administrative centres, officials, military resources and communication routes.

Key chronological relationships

PeriodMajor development
6th–4th centuries BCEMagadha emerged as a dominant mahajanapada.
4th century BCEThe Nandas consolidated and expanded Magadhan power.
326 BCEAlexander's army refused to advance beyond the Beas.
c. 321 BCEChandragupta founded the Mauryan Empire.
c. 305–303 BCEChandragupta reached a settlement with Seleucus I Nicator.
c. 298–273 BCEBindusara ruled and maintained the Mauryan Empire.
c. 268–232 BCEAshoka's reign, using a commonly accepted approximate chronology.
c. 261 BCEAshoka's conquest of Kalinga, dated to his 8th year after coronation.

The precise years used for early Mauryan accession, succession and coronation vary slightly between historical reconstructions. The dates above are conventional approximations, while the relative sequence of rulers and the distinction between Chandragupta's foundation of the empire and Ashoka's Kalinga conquest are secure.

Prelims focus

  • Girnar near Junagadh contains Ashoka's Major Rock Edicts.
  • Pushyagupta constructed Sudarshana Lake during Chandragupta Maurya's reign, according to the later inscription.
  • Tushaspha improved the lake during Ashoka's reign.
  • Rudradaman I recorded repairs around 150 CE.
  • Skandagupta was associated with another repair in the 5th century CE.
  • Trap: The Girnar rock preserves inscriptions from different dynasties and periods; all of them are not contemporary with Ashoka.

[Sources: NCERT, Themes in Indian History, Part I, Class 12, Theme 2, Kings, Farmers and Towns, printed pp. 31–38, including the section on Sudarshana Lake; NCERT, Our Pasts–I, Class 6, Chapters 6 and 8, printed pp. 59–61 and 75–81; Shubhra Pramanik, Significant Discoveries around Sudarshan Lake, Junagadh, Puratattva, Number 35, 2004–2005, printed pp. 179–181, Indian Archaeological Society, digital copy hosted by IGNCA, consulted 18 November 2026; P. Bhaskar Reddy, The Mauryan Empire, Outlines of Indian History, section 5.1, INFLIBNET, consulted 18 November 2026.]

data.description: Genuine documentary photograph of the Girnar inscription rock near Junagadh, Gujarat, clearly showing the boulder and its inscribed surface. This rock bears 14 Major Rock Edicts of Ashoka and later inscriptions of Rudradaman I and Skandagupta. Do not substitute a pillar or another monument.

pictures.alt: Mauryan governors Pushyagupta and Tushaspha constructed and improved Sudarshana Lake; later repairs involved Rudradaman I and Skandagupta.
pictures.caption: The Sudarshana Lake record connects early Mauryan construction with later repairs.

title: Mauryan Gujarat: Girnar, Sudarshana Lake and the Complete Political Sequence
